why_not_pass: This is a baseline, not a verdict. No performance budget has been agreed, so nothing can pass or fail. The numbers come from a Linux container over loopback on nearly empty workspaces, in Chromium only, and were measured by the author alone.

observations.claim_class: COMPUTED from rc8/performance_baselines.json, at 1280 CSS pixels unless stated
items: First start of a never-run tree: aguayluz-pr 9383.2 ms and moneysweep-pr 9506.3 ms; every other application under 1600 ms. One observation each, not a distribution. The cause is not established here.
Later starts on an empty workspace: every application between about 350 ms and 1060 ms at the median. aguayluz-pr is the slowest (about 1060 ms).

JavaScript loaded up front (gzip): skywatcher-pr 582240 bytes and ovnis-pr 500160 bytes, each a single file holding the whole application; moneysweep-pr 259059 bytes. The other five are between about 90,000 and 136,000 bytes and load the rest later.

aguayluz-pr transfers a median of about 10 MB per route and 29 MB on /map. Its built JavaScript is 0.8 MB gzip in total, so most of that is data fetched by the pages, not the build. Which requests carry it was not broken down.
thehub-pr /gis?view=digital-twin transfers about 8.2 MB; the next largest thehub-pr routes about 2.4 MB.
Median largest-contentful-paint per route is between about 115 ms and 520 ms for every application in this harness. aguayluz-pr has three routes just over 1000 ms.

The local server sends files uncompressed, so bytes transferred track raw size, not gzip size. For a desktop application on loopback that costs little; it would matter if an application were served over a network.
Layout shift is 0 at the median for every application; aguayluz-pr and moneysweep-pr each have a route above 0.1.

pilot_branches_against_main.reading: Build size and transfer are effectively unchanged. Timing differences are smaller than the run-to-run spread, so no timing change, in either direction, can be claimed.
pilot_branches_against_main.not_comparable: first_run: the pilot trees had been run before; the main trees had not.

unreliable.note: Cells whose timing runs differ by more than 50% of the median are flagged in the artifact and should not be quoted individually.
unreliable.across_route_lcp: The spread of per-route LCP medians within an application is wide (relative spread above 1 for four applications), so an application-level LCP median hides slow routes; the per-route rows are the evidence.

proposed_budgets_for_decision.status: NOT ADOPTED. Offered for the user to accept, change or reject. Nothing in this package is judged against them.
proposed_budgets_for_decision.basis: Chosen so that most applications sit inside them today and the outliers named in the observations sit outside. They are bounds for this harness, not device targets.

device_timings.note: Needs real hardware; the macOS startup delay reported earlier is not addressed by these numbers.
